kjv: Neither shall he regard the God of his fathers
mine: He shall pay no attention to the gods of his fathers
note: elohe avotav, said of a Seleucid king (Antiochus IV) who neglected his ancestral Greek gods for Zeus Olympios, is naturally plural; KJV's singular capitalised "God" has fed the idea of a Jewish apostate antichrist.
eloah ma'uzzim is "god of strongholds/fortresses" (often linked to Zeus or Jupiter Capitolinus); "forces" now suggests military power or natural forces in general.
rabbot can be "many (fem.)" or repointed ribbot "tens of thousands"; KJV's italic "countries" is a supply the Hebrew does not specify.
